_meta.block_range_note: The 46-block pinned research window 25612655..25612701. Bounded on purpose: this event has 58,006 instances all-time and a full-history request is refused ('Query returned more than 50000 results').
_meta.note: AcquisitionRequested(uint256 indexed requestId, address indexed requester, uint256 acquisitionFee, uint256 totalWeight). The two non-indexed data words carry acquisitionFee and totalWeight, so a COMPLETE price history is reconstructable from events alone with no archive state access. Verified below against the pinned eth_call reads.
_meta.raw_body_note: Raw log array lives at response.result (the untouched JSON-RPC body). It is deliberately NOT duplicated at a top-level 'logs' key.

cross_check_against_state._note: PROOF that a price history rebuilt from AcquisitionRequested is exact, not approximate. The FIRST AcquisitionRequested log in block N carries the pool state as of the END of block N-1, bit-for-bit -- provided no other FWA state-mutating tx precedes it inside block N. Verified on 7 of 8 consecutive blocks sampled in this window; the one exception (block 25612669) had an earlier state-mutating tx in the same block, which is exactly why a consumer must order by (blockNumber, logIndex) and must NOT assume one event per block.

counter_example_end_of_block_25612701._note: Do NOT compare an event to the state at the END of its own block. The last AcquisitionRequested in block 25612701 reads 136237209948799268 while acquisitionFee() at that block reads 136260883651302691 -- the pool moved later in the same block. A 0.017% error, easy to mistake for a rounding bug.
